findings.F1: Inside the falling calm profile, the plan's measure has no slope on its own side, and the whole spread comes from the other side. On the explore windows' non-overlapping 5-day grid, coins with a positive 5-day scaled push rose only +0.96 % more than their drift over the next 5 days (48 cases). Within those positive pushes the slope was flat (t 0.04). Coins with a zero or negative push lagged by −3.26 % (73 cases; Welch t 2.34), and that lag kept growing: −4.04 % at 10 days and −5.90 % at 20 days.
findings.F2: The market rewards a longer push over a longer horizon than the plan tested, and only inside the profile. The 10-day scaled return predicts the next 10 days with slope 1.25 % per unit and t 2.73 (111 cases). The 3-day scaled return predicts the next 10 and 20 days with t 2.18 and 2.19. The plan's own 5-day push over 5 days gives t 1.53 (121 cases). Outside the profile, every one of these pairs has a t between −0.74 and 0.83 (492 to 593 cases), so the effect belongs to falling calm markets, as the brief says.
findings.F3: The quintiles show the steps sit at the bottom, not at the top. The two lowest 5-day-push quintiles lagged by −4.7 % and −4.1 % over 5 days, and by −5.4 % and −5.2 % over 10 days. The two highest gained +1.7 % and +0.3 % over 5 days. The top quintile gained +1.5 % over 10 days and +9.4 % over 20 days, but on only 25 cases.
findings.F4: The slope over 10 days is larger the deeper the coin's 60-day fall. In the deepest third (mean −43 %) and the middle third (−26 %), the slope was 2.12 % with t 1.89 and 1.89 % with t 2.04 (about 30 cases each). In the shallowest third (−16 %) it was 0.56 % with t 0.35.
findings.F5: The effect is uneven across years and coins. The 10-day slope was positive in 2018 (t 2.15) and 2021 (t 1.48) and negative in 2019 (t −1.42). By coin, ETH carries it (10-day t 2.12), while XMR and ZEC are weak (t 0.38 and 0.37). Every coin with enough cases shows the negative-push lag over 10 days, from −3.5 % to −7.3 %.

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, a coin's 10-day return divided by the standard deviation of its daily returns over the last 30 days predicts its rise over the next 10 days: the larger this scaled push upward, the larger the rise that follows, and the weaker or more negative it is, the smaller the rise.
ideas.consequence: In a calm decline, a long trader would favour coins whose last ten days rose strongly for their usual swing and hold about ten days, staying away from coins whose recent return is still weak.
ideas.name: calm decline ten-day push

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, a coin's 5-day return divided by the standard deviation of its daily returns over the last 30 days predicts its rise over the next 10 days, and the deeper the coin's 60-day fall, the larger the rise that follows a given scaled push.
ideas.consequence: A strong scaled push after a deep calm decline is a reason to buy and hold about ten days, more than the same push after a shallow decline.
ideas.name: deep calm decline push
